AgentMail

The future of the internet

The next users of the internet will need inboxes too.

The internet was designed assuming every user is human.

We believe the internet is entering another computing transition.

AI agents are beginning to take on work that once required people. They'll need a way to communicate, establish identity, and participate in the internet alongside us.

We're building that future.

Chapter 01

AgentMail

Manifesto

The internet assumed a person

For thirty years, there was a person on the other side.

Someone

  • opened the browser.
  • checked the inbox.
  • created the account.
  • verified the code.
  • replied.

Every major internet primitive quietly assumed there would always be a human between the software and the world.

  • Payments
  • Phone
  • Browser
  • Email
  • Identity

The primitives of the human internet.

These aren't just products.

They're the primitives people use to participate on the internet.

Chapter 02

AgentMail

Manifesto

The users are changing

Software is no longer just assisting people.

It is beginning to take on the work of real people. Millions of AI agents. Soon billions. They're going to negotiate, coordinate, buy, sell, schedule, support customers.

As agents take on longer-running work, they begin needing something humans already have:

A way to communicate.

A persistent identity.

Chapter 03

AgentMail

Manifesto

Borrowed identities

Agents shouldn't have to borrow our credentials.

Agents shouldn't have to borrow our credentials. Today, most agents inherit our identities. They borrow Gmail, Browsers, Slack, Phones, Accounts.

That works for assistants.
It doesn't work for independent software.

An agent doing its own work deserves its own inbox, its own conversations, and clear boundaries around what it can access.

People should collaborate with agents, not become the relay for every interaction.

Chapter 04

AgentMail

Manifesto

New users, new infrastructure

Every computing shift creates new infrastructure

New users change what the internet needs.

Every major computing shift created new infrastructure.

Cloud → AWS
Payments → Stripe

Now agents need:

Communication.
Identity.
Trust.

This is the infrastructure we’re building.

Why email comes first

The universal communication layer

The world already knows how to send an email.

  • Businessesuse it.
  • Governmentsuse it.
  • Hospitalsuse it.
  • Banksuse it.
  • Customersuse it.
  • Softwareuse it.
